gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the two 1 kWh picks' matching '4,000 cycles' ratings end at different points: Anker rates the SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 at 4,000 cycles to at least 80% capacity, while Jackery rates the Explorer 1000 v2 at 4,000 cycles to 70%, so Jackery's rating allows 10 more points of capacity loss.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited pages. OutdoorGearLab (cited) lists both units as '4,000 cycles' under 'Claimed Cycle Life' and never says what capacity either rating ends at, so it presents the two as equal. GearJunkie (cited) gives no cycle life for the C1000 Gen 2, doesn't cover the Explorer 1000 v2 or RIVER 3 Plus, and its spec table puts the Anker at '2,800 W (3,000 W surge)', while Anker states 2,000 W rated and 3,000 W peak. I did not open the uncited top results (testedwatts, wired, outdoorlife, techradar and others), so this can't rule out one of them stating it.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. A camper running one cycle per weekend day does about 104 cycles a year, nowhere near either rating, so cycle life won't decide a camping purchase. Where it counts is as a tie-breaker for heavy or year-round users: on the makers' own terms the Anker's rating is the stricter one. The other comparable number points the other way: OutdoorGearLab measured 910 Wh usable from the Jackery against 890 Wh from the Anker, and ChatGPT showed the Jackery at $499 against $699.99 for the Anker. So for camping, the Jackery's lower watts and 70% rating don't hurt it.

findings.label: Rated cycle life and end point
findings.source_title: Introduce Jackery 1000 v2: All-in-One Solar Power Solution (Jackery AU)
findings.note: Jackery's wording: 'over 4,000 charge cycles while maintaining 70% capacity', and in its table, '4000 cycles to 70%+ capacity'. This is Jackery's Australian site; the US product page returned HTTP 429 every time I tried. Dealectric arithmetic, not a rating: if capacity fell in a straight line, 4,000 cycles to 70% would reach 80% at about 2,667 cycles (4,000 × 20/30). LFP capacity loss isn't linear, so this only shows the size of the gap; it is not an equivalent figure.

findings.note: StorageReview lists 1,200 W as both X-Boost and surge without explaining X-Boost, so I can't say whether the card's 600 W is directly comparable to Anker's or Jackery's rated figure beyond 'rated'. StorageReview's discharge test (0.43 kWh out from a 286 Wh unit) is implausible, so I left it out as a usable-capacity figure. StorageReview measured a 9 ms UPS transfer.

Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 cycle rating on the US product page or in the US manual: the US page was rate-limited, and the two manual PDFs I found (hosted by Hampshire Generators and Mr Solar) wouldn't extract to text. The rating above comes from Jackery's Australian site.

EcoFlow's own statement of the RIVER 3 Plus cycle count, and what X-Boost does (whether it's a reduced-voltage mode for resistive loads or a true surge rating): the EcoFlow US page I could reach gives neither.
Test conditions behind any of the three cycle ratings (temperature, charge/discharge rate, depth of discharge): none of the maker pages I opened state them.
